entries.subject: DAMIT 129: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-129.txt. Model 129, version 2011-03-28, pole (275°, 51°), period 12.17458 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 107 ±10 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the selected archive model has a physical size calibration. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 116.46 ± 1.14 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 34 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model surveys: body-specific candidate not established
entries.finding: The imported survey cites Hanuš 2017, Viikinkoski 2017 and Vernazza 2021 without identifying a selected product for this body. The current DAMIT reference join does not bind selected model 129 to those surveys. This does not prove that no resolved model exists elsewhere; a body-specific candidate and its release must be identified before the entry can count as included.
entries.revisitWhen: A target row, supplementary model or release URL from one of these surveys establishes a concrete candidate and permits comparison with the selected shape.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — size comparison candidates; an independent fit or occultation ellipsoid is not silently equated with this mesh’s volume.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 128, pole ['94', '35'], [Model 128](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/128) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 128: pole (94°, 35°), 12.17458 h, version 2011-03-28, archive diameter 96 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
